summary: Retested Prep Agent through the public URL. The focused Prep APIs are responsive and non-blocking: POST 0.092s, immediate list GET 0.067s, and detail GET 0.067s; the workflow entered processing without the prior cross-event-loop failure. Production UI access is still blocked because the required test account returns trial_expired and redirects /prep-agent to /pricing. With only the subscription-status gate isolated in Playwright, the real Prep Agent page and APIs passed: page rendered without the ErrorBoundary, all form controls worked, and UI POST returned in 0.170s.

minor.issue: The required test@school.edu account still returns has_access=false/status=trial_expired, contrary to the requested active subscription setup; this caused 1 of 4 focused pytest tests to fail and blocks production UI access.

integration_issues.issue: The real production flow redirects to /pricing because the required account is trial_expired. Prep Agent runtime behavior passed only in a diagnostic browser run that mocked /api/subscription/status as active while keeping classes, batches, notifications, create, and delete APIs real.

issues: Week Starts uses the browser-native input[type=date] rather than the app's shadcn calendar/popover component, resulting in browser-dependent date-picker UX.

action_items: Update the public-environment subscription record for test@school.edu to active or trialing with a valid future end date, then rerun the unmocked /prep-agent browser flow.
Consider replacing the native date input with the standard shadcn calendar component.
Add an explicit UI error state for initial Prep Agent data-load failures instead of only logging to the console.
critical_code_review_comments: The new run_llm_in_executor boundary correctly keeps Mongo/Motor operations on the server event loop while running only each LLM SDK call in the thread pool; the prior cross-loop failure was not reproduced.

PrepAgent.js no longer references the undefined fetchBatches function; polling consistently calls fetchBatchesUpdate and the page rendered without the Something went wrong boundary in the isolated subscription diagnostic.

fetchData catches initial classes/batches/notifications failures and only console.error logs them, then clears loading; users would see misleading empty form/list states without an error or retry control.
routes/prep_agent.py is 897 lines and should be split into route, workflow, prompt/standards, and publishing modules.

success_rate.backend: 75% (3/4 focused tests passed; all Prep Agent endpoint tests passed, subscription access setup failed)
success_rate.frontend: 0% unmocked requested route access; 100% isolated Prep Agent page/form/create/delete diagnostic after mocking only the broken subscription gate

seed_data_creation: Created uniquely named TEST_ Prep Agent batches in pytest and the isolated UI run; both were deleted during cleanup.
test_credentials: Read /app/memory/test_credentials.md and authenticated successfully with the required teacher account; subscription status remains trial_expired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use the public URL from frontend/.env. Focused API tests are in test_prep_agent.py. Current measured API latencies are POST 0.092s/list GET 0.067s/detail GET 0.067s, and no cross-event-loop failure occurred. Unmocked browser navigation still lands on /pricing. The diagnostic browser run mocked only subscription/status and then used real Prep APIs; it rendered all fields and created a batch in 0.170s. Five checkbox data-testid attributes and delete-selected-batch-btn were added for maintainable retesting.
rca_of_the_issue: ProtectedRoute calls /api/subscription/status before mounting PrepAgent. That endpoint finds no active/trialing subscription for the required user and the user's initial trial period has elapsed, so it returns has_access=false/status=trial_expired; ProtectedRoute then intentionally redirects to /pricing. The Prep Agent responsiveness defect itself appears fixed because only LLM calls now execute in the thread pool while async Mongo operations remain on the main server loop.
